title: K6: load testing as JavaScript code

videos.script: Lesson 4 built a test plan in a window, and saved it as XML. {{jmeter}} This lesson writes the test as a program instead. A short JavaScript file, run by one tool called k6. {{file}} A test in a file can be read in a code review. A diff of it says what changed, in words. {{diff}} First, the smallest test there is: five virtual users asking for one show for ten seconds. {{first}} Then a real journey through the box office. Look at a show, think for a moment, book a seat. {{journey}} Sometimes the seat is already taken, and the answer is 409. That is the box office working, not failing, and the script says so. {{conflict}} Then the requirement from lesson 1 goes into the file, as thresholds. {{thresholds}} At three journeys a second, every threshold holds and k6 exits with zero. {{pass}} At thirty, the bookings queue up, two thresholds are crossed, and the exit code is ninety-nine. {{fail}} No request failed, and every check passed. The run still failed, because it was too slow. {{slow}} Last, the summary k6 prints at the end, read one line at a time. {{summary}}
